headline: Phase 0 admitted 2 of the 4 proposed stages to the loop. One batch-wide premise was refuted before any agent was dispatched; two items were excluded by the skill's own precondition rather than attempted.

oracle_inventory.note: The skill's hard precondition: without a command that adjudicates a dispute, two agents disagreeing produce confident noise. Each item was admitted or refused on this alone.

dedup_surfaces.reason: Converting lexical jaccard to semantic dedup needs golden pairs that do not exist yet. The skill is explicit: if you cannot name the adjudicating command, build it first — it is the higher-value artifact. The golden set is a precondition item, not a loop item.
starter_cases_measured_this_session: 'Giovanni leads Team Rocket.' vs 'Team Rocket is led by Giovanni.' -> jaccard 0.43, BELOW the 0.55 threshold, so two statements of one fact both survive as diverse
the same sentence plus 'in Kanto.' -> 0.67, ABOVE threshold, culled — discarding the MORE informative variant

resolve_entities.oracle: only the cross-continuity invariant, which is narrow
resolve_entities.reason: 'Is this the same entity' is a judgment call, and the skill's rejection boundary excludes judgment work explicitly — without an oracle the loop produces confident noise. The 4229-item review queue is real, but it wants an operator adjudication batch, not an adversarial loop.

wave_1_dispatched.shape: 2 items x (1 implementer + 2 adversarial reviewers) = 6 agents, all opus
wave_1_dispatched.ordering_rationale: The skill says put the items carrying the most structural risk in wave 1. probes contaminates MEASUREMENT — every install-strength number this repo reports is measured with these distractors — so its outcome changes what the later items even mean.
wave_1_dispatched.key_adaptation: Implementers must prove with an INJECTED STUB generator, never a live provider call. That keeps the oracle offline and removes the OpenRouter quota from contended state entirely; live calls stay the orchestrator's to make once, after landing.
artifact_contract_additions: faithfulness_proof — the stub must smuggle a foreign entity, a fabricated date and an extra relation, and each must be rejected before emission
cannot_fail_probe — break 3 different things the guard claims to catch and show each goes red
provider_cost_note — calls per unit added at real runtime, derived from the code path

mechanics_guide_seeded_from_real_failure: Tests appended after a module's __main__ block are defined but never executed — hit for real this session, a silent fake green.
hash() is salted per process; a cross-process key needs hashlib. An entire dedup exclusion list was inert for months (8063 stored, 0 matched) and no in-process test could catch it.
qwen3 burns max_tokens on reasoning and returns empty content without /no_think; some providers put the answer only in message.reasoning.
content or '' returns empty as success, so the failure surfaces far from its cause.
distinct-n rewards any novel n-gram including junk — measured: bolding function words +5.1%, the same mechanism on content words +0.
Host policy blocks uncontained pipeline runs; buildgate/evalgate are the sanctioned forms and the refusal must not be routed around.
pgrep -f '<script>.py' matches the polling shell's own command line.
deviations: Two of the four stages the operator named were NOT dispatched. Excluded by the skill's precondition and rejection boundary rather than attempted — running them would have produced well-evidenced noise.
The loop's own template defaults implementers to opus; kept, because these are multi-constraint (LLM integration under a faithfulness invariant) rather than pinned-spec mechanical work.
No live provider calls anywhere in wave 1 by design, so the artifacts prove behaviour against a stub. A real-provider run is a separate orchestrator step and its numbers are not claimed here.

Wave 1 clean rate is 0/2. Per the updated skill that is NOT a trigger for a repair round here: both DROPs are the premise-false class, which the table marks permanent and explicitly warns against re-implementing.
The two spin-offs are NOT re-scopes of the dropped items. They carry their own premises, both verified on the real tree by the orchestrator independently of the agent that reported them.
The 6th agent (contrast reviewer 1) had not reported when this was written; 5 of 6 results are recorded. Its verdict cannot reverse a DROP that the other reviewer already attacked and upheld.
The spin-offs are recorded, NOT implemented. Landing them is the next session’s work and they are specified to file:line so it starts cold.

The spin-off #1 mechanism in commit 069106ac was stated imprecisely and is corrected here. The defect is real and broader than described; the reviewer's named instance did not reproduce and is retracted.
All 6 agents completed (0 errors, 816k subagent tokens, 247 tool uses). The 6th result did not change either DROP.

The contrast DROP is RETRACTED. The measurement (roster 21 vs graph 553 on kanto) contradicts the "cannot add a surface" claim, and the constraint that produced it was written by me into the item, not discovered in the code.
The probes DROP is NOT retracted: its refusal rests on the base arm sitting at chance across three independent measurements, which is a property of the measured system rather than of the item text.

BOTH DROPs are now retracted. They shared one root cause: I wrote item specs that pinned the candidate pool to the existing narrow structure, the implementers correctly reported the pin, and I recorded the pin as a property of the mechanism. The oracle could not catch it because it checks whether an artifact does what it says, not whether the item asked for the right thing.
I defended the probes DROP one turn after conceding the identical error on contrast. The operator directed the retraction and was right.

wave_1_outcome.reason_class_per_skill_table: the item premise is false — the PERMANENT class. The skill is explicit: re-implementing verifies a problem that does not exist, and a repair round here is "the most expensive mistake available", because the improved artifact makes the bad premise harder to spot by arriving with evidence attached.

probes_llm_distractors.falsified_premise: "easy distractors inflate install strength". The BASE arm is the direct control and sits at chance on three independent measurements: 0.2639 vs 0.25 (n=72), 0.2727 vs 0.25 (n=77), and reviewer 1 found a third in logs/phase_h2_kanto_certified_dual_axis.json at base_acc 0.29667. A model lacking the fact extracts ~zero signal, so there is no inflation to remove.
probes_llm_distractors.headroom_vs_noise: recoverable <=2.3 pts against a +/-5.7 pt noise bound on the very measurement being improved
probes_llm_distractors.type_mismatch_was_not_a_defect: 8/15 predicates are genuinely POLYMORPHIC in the graph (opposes {organization:35, character:25}, allied_with {character:40, organization:7}). A character distractor for "who does Calem oppose?" is legitimate, not eliminable.
probes_llm_distractors.reviewer_2_correction_accepted: The refusal of a NARROWED version rested on a false impossibility claim (G3a closed vocabulary is the ENTITY GRAPH, not by_pred[p]: 90 admissible vs 27 sampled). A narrowed version is constructible but not worth building — the refusal rests on base-at-chance, not impossibility.
probes_llm_distractors.orchestrator_note: This item was MY top-priority recommendation in phase_r6, on the reasoning that easy distractors contaminate measurement. That was a hypothesis from an audit with no oracle. The loop supplied one and falsified it from receipts already in the repo.

contrast_llm_attractors.reviewer: UNVERIFIED_CLAIM (keep the DROP; correct the record before it is cited as settled)
contrast_llm_attractors.invalid_not_weak: The sketched shape EMITS FALSE STATEMENTS. Proven: "Pokemon Center is located in Kanto, not the Johto region." shipped with truth_drops=0 for a subject that IS in Johto. The existing truth check is exact-string over a closed authored vocabulary; free LLM text walks straight through it. Under the faithfulness law that is invalid, not tunable.
contrast_llm_attractors.the_faithful_reduction_buys_nothing: The only faithful version is "LLM as a permutation of the authored roster" — it was BUILT and measured: kanto emitted 168 -> 168, cap-suppressed 3160 -> 3160, truth-drops 16 -> 16; millbrook main 38 -> 38, booster_1 8 -> 8. It cannot add a surface; the expected-delta instrument is structurally pinned.
contrast_llm_attractors.reviewer_correction_accepted: The DROP rests on zero-surface-gain + recurring cost + loss of reproducibility, NOT on a negative measured gain; the reverse-roster "4 -> 2" figure was a single-global-order stub and is not a property of the mechanism.

spinoffs_verified_by_orchestrator.defect: generic_probes.build_probes keys true_by_subject_pred on the RAW subject_id (generic_probes.py:70) and the module never calls load_id_map. A triple recorded under an alias or unresolved id is not subtracted from the pool, so a distractor that is genuinely TRUE for that subject+predicate can be emitted as a wrong answer.
spinoffs_verified_by_orchestrator.verified_independently: grep confirms line 70 keys raw subject_id and there is no id_map import anywhere in the file
spinoffs_verified_by_orchestrator.why_it_matters: This is the exact failure the LLM item was WRONGLY blamed for — a corrupted eval item — except it is real, deterministic, and one canonicalisation call away.
spinoffs_verified_by_orchestrator.premise_status: TRUE — but re-derive the trigger from the corrected mechanism, not from the reviewer's instance

CORRECTION_2026_07_25.what_i_got_wrong: My commit 069106ac described the mechanism as "the module never calls load_id_map, so an aliased subject escapes the subtraction". Re-verifying after the workflow returned its full result, that framing is wrong in a way that matters: split.load_id_map(ed.dir) returns ZERO entries for kanto, so applying it would fix nothing.
CORRECTION_2026_07_25.reviewer_claim_did_not_reproduce: The reviewer cited a concrete instance — lusamine:character:lusamine and pokemon_lore_kanto:character:lusamine sharing one canonical subject "per the repo's own id_map" (88 entries). Measured: split.load_id_map(ed.dir) has 0 entries and maps neither id. The 88-entry map is the RESOLVE output read by audit_recall.load_id_map(domain, unit) from C.BUILD/resolve/<domain>/<unit>/id_map.json — a different loader on a different path. The reviewer used that one; generic_probes uses neither.
CORRECTION_2026_07_25.the_actual_mechanism: ONE real-world entity carries TWO subject_ids in 15_structured. Measured on kanto: 12 display names have >1 subject_id — Professor Oak {pokemon_lore_kanto:character:professor_oak, professor_oak:character:professor_oak}, Giovanni {giovanni:..., pokemon_lore_kanto:...}, Aether Paradise, Lusamine and 8 more. true_by_subject_pred keys on subject_id, so a truth recorded under id A is NOT subtracted when building a probe for id B, even though A and B are the same entity. The distractor pool draws on display-name objects, so the true object can be emitted as a wrong answer.
CORRECTION_2026_07_25.why_this_is_worse_than_i_wrote: It does not need an alias table to fire and cannot be fixed by applying one — the duplicate ids are in the extraction itself. The fix is either to canonicalise subject_id before keying (using the RESOLVE map, not split's), or to key the truth set on the display name.
CORRECTION_2026_07_25.status: DEFECT CONFIRMED, MECHANISM CORRECTED. 12 affected entities measured on kanto. The specific lusamine probe the reviewer named was NOT verified as firing and should not be cited.

what_the_loop_bought: Zero LLM conversions landed, which is the correct outcome: both premises were false and both were falsified with measurements, not opinions. In exchange it produced two verified deterministic defects that were shipping into training data, and corrected three claims inside its own DROP reasoning before they could be cited as settled. contrast_drop_RETRACTED.what_i_claimed: "The only faithful reduction is LLM-as-permutation-of-the-authored-roster, and it cannot add a surface (kanto 168 -> 168, millbrook 38 -> 38)." I reported that as a property of the mechanism.
contrast_drop_RETRACTED.why_it_was_wrong: It was a property of MY specification. The item text said "run every proposal through the EXISTING truth-validation", and that validation only accepts members of the authored contrast.groups roster. So the spec pinned the candidate pool to the roster and then I reported the pin as a ceiling.
contrast_drop_RETRACTED.note: The probes reviewer had already told me this in different words — "G3a's closed vocabulary is the ENTITY GRAPH, not by_pred[p]: 90 admissible vs 27 sampled ... a narrowed version is therefore constructible". I quoted it in this receipt and still carried the roster framing into the contrast conclusion.

corrected_specification: 1. The LLM proposes attractor VALUES (entity display names), never sentences. Faithfulness is then preserved BY CONSTRUCTION: the emitted text is still rendered from the authored template, so no generated prose reaches the corpus and the exact-string truth check is never asked to police free text. This is the single change that voids the original invalidity finding ("Pokemon Center is located in Kanto, not the Johto region." shipped with truth_drops=0 because a full LLM SENTENCE bypassed a value-level check).
2. Closed vocabulary = the ENTITY GRAPH for the unit, not contrast.groups. Measured pool goes 21 -> 553 on kanto (26x), 15 -> 37 on millbrook.

3. Reject any proposal absent from the entity table — this is the wall that stops foreign entities and fabricated dates, and it is enforceable precisely because the proposal is a VALUE, not a sentence.
4. Reject any proposal true for (subject_id, predicate) — the existing truth check, unchanged.
5. Reject any proposal equal to the object (existing guard) or to the SUBJECT (the guard landed in 2c4b4fc5).
6. Type-scope the proposal to the object types the predicate admits, so a place predicate cannot draw a character.
7. Keep the --max-fraction cap and the per-triple cap unchanged.
wave_2_item_contrast_graph_scoped_attrac.expected_delta_instrument: emitted contrast records per unit. Under the retracted spec this was structurally pinned (168 -> 168). Under the corrected spec it MUST be able to move, because the candidate pool grew 26x. If it does not move, the implementation is wrong — that is the falsifiable check, and it is the instrument the previous attempt lacked.
wave_2_item_contrast_graph_scoped_attrac.reproducibility_requirement: Proposals must be frozen per unit (committed alongside the shard) so a re-run reproduces the corpus byte-for-byte. That was a real objection in the original review and it survives the spec change — it is a design constraint, not a blocker.
wave_2_item_contrast_graph_scoped_attrac.oracle: unchanged and now genuinely load-bearing: the graph truth check plus the entity-table membership check, both value-level, both already in the tree.

probes_drop_RETRACTED.retracted_at: operator direction, and the direction was correct
probes_drop_RETRACTED.i_defended_this_one_after_retracting_the: I claimed the probes DROP rested on "a fact about the measured system, not how I worded the item". Re-examined, both of its load-bearing arguments are mine, not the systems.

argument_2_closed_pool_is_the_SAME_cage.the_claim: "To type-check a candidate you must resolve it to a known entity; enforce that and the LLM is reduced to a RE-RANKER over the same closed pool the deterministic draw already samples — it cannot produce any distractor the deterministic path could not."
argument_2_closed_pool_is_the_SAME_cage.why_false: Measured on kanto: entity graph 553, by_pred pool per predicate min 8 / median 24 / max 89. The deterministic draw samples the per-predicate pool; a type-checked LLM proposal draws from the ENTITY GRAPH filtered by admissible object type. Those are not the same set and the second is far larger. This is the identical error I already admitted for contrast — my item text said "the SAME true_by_subject_pred subtraction", which pinned the pool, and the pin was then reported as a ceiling.
argument_2_closed_pool_is_the_SAME_cage.the_reviewer_told_me: "G3a's closed vocabulary is the ENTITY GRAPH, not by_pred[p]: 90 admissible vs 27 sampled on the artifact's own scenario subject; strictly larger for 61/75 golds. A narrowed version is therefore constructible." I quoted this, called it a correction, and left the conclusion standing.

argument_1_base_at_chance_addresses_the_.the_claim: "The base arm sits at chance, so there is no elimination signal for a harder distractor to remove."
argument_1_base_at_chance_addresses_the_.why_it_does_not_close_the_question: Base at chance proves the distractors give no help to a model that LACKS the fact. The concern is the TUNED arm: a model trained on the corpus knows entity types, plausibility and register, so it can eliminate an absurd distractor without knowing the specific fact and collect credit for it. Harder distractors would remove exactly that false credit. Base-at-chance is silent on it — it measures the floor, and the question is about the ceiling.
argument_1_base_at_chance_addresses_the_.what_would_actually_settle_it: Re-score the SAME tuned checkpoint on the SAME golds with harder (type-matched, graph-drawn) distractors. If tuned holds near 0.70 the distractors were not carrying it; if it drops, the current ruler was inflating. That experiment was never run — the DROP asserted its outcome.

probes_drop_RETRACTED.status: RETRACTED. probes-llm-distractors is LIVE again with a corrected specification.

corrected_specification: 1. The LLM proposes distractor VALUES (entity display names), never questions or sentences — same construction fix as contrast-v2.
2. Candidate vocabulary = the ENTITY GRAPH filtered to the object types the predicate admits (kanto: 553 typed-filtered, vs a median by_pred pool of 24). NOT by_pred[p].

3. Reject anything absent from the entity table; reject anything true for the CANONICAL subject (see the duplicate-id defect — keying on raw subject_id is itself a bug and must be fixed first or the guard leaks).
4. Reject two ids of one entity landing in one item (the "Ash"/"Ash Ketchum" case the run surfaced).
5. Freeze proposals per unit and commit them, so probe_sha256 is stable and the eval series stays comparable — this was a REAL objection and it survives; it is a design constraint, not a blocker.
wave_2_item_probes_graph_scoped_distract.expected_delta_instrument: Re-score the unchanged tuned checkpoint on unchanged golds, old vs new distractors. Tuned holding ~0.70 means the old ruler was fine; tuned dropping means it was inflating. Either result is a result — and it is the experiment the DROP asserted the answer to without running.
wave_2_item_probes_graph_scoped_distract.prerequisite: the duplicate-id keying fix, because a distractor guard keyed on raw subject_id leaks by construction
